At considerable effort and expense, Hammer obtained the specified artifacts within the two-week period. When Hammer requested payment, Kay refused. Kay claimed that there was no consideration for the promise. Hammer would prevail against Kay based on

choices.label: A
choices.text: Unilateral contract

choices.label: B
choices.text: Unjust enrichment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Public policy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Quasi-contract

questions.explanation: Kay's promise invited acceptance by performance rather than by a return promise, so it was an offer for a unilateral contract. When Hammer completed the requested act within two weeks, the offer was accepted and a binding contract was formed; Hammer's performance is the bargained-for consideration for Kay's promise (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§45, 71). Unjust enrichment and quasi-contract are remedies implied by law only when there is no enforceable contract, and here an actual contract exists. Public policy is not a basis for Hammer's claim because nothing about the agreement is illegal or contrary to public policy.
questions.explanationJa: Kay の約束は、相手の約束ではなく行為の完了による承諾を求めるもので、片務契約（unilateral contract）の申込みです。Hammer が2週間以内に指定の美術品を入手した時点で承諾があったことになり、契約が成立します。Hammer の行為が Kay の約束に対する取引上の約因（consideration）になります。不当利得（unjust enrichment）や準契約（quasi-contract）は、有効な契約が存在しない場合に法が認める救済なので、契約が成立している本問では根拠になりません。合意に違法性や公序違反の要素はないため、公序（public policy）も Hammer の請求の根拠ではありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.8

questions.stem: On June 1, Year 2, Decker orally guaranteed the payment of a $5,000 note Decker's cousin owed Baker. Decker's agreement with Baker provided that Decker's guaranty would terminate in 18 months. On June 3, Year 2, Baker wrote Decker confirming Decker's guaranty. Decker did not object to the confirmation. On August 23, Year 2, Decker's cousin defaulted on the note and Baker demanded that Decker honor the guaranty. Decker refused. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decker is liable under the oral guaranty because Decker did not object to Baker's June 3 letter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decker is not liable under the oral guaranty because it expired more than one year after June 1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decker is liable under the oral guaranty because Baker demanded payment within one year of the date the guaranty was given.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decker is not liable under the oral guaranty because Decker's promise was not in writing.

questions.explanation: A promise to answer for the debt of another (a suretyship or guaranty promise) is within the statute of frauds and is enforceable only if evidenced by a writing signed by the promisor, unless the main purpose of the promise is to benefit the promisor (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§110, 112, 116). Decker guaranteed a cousin's debt and received no direct benefit, and Decker never signed a writing, so the guaranty is unenforceable against Decker. Decker's failure to object to Baker's June 3 letter does not satisfy the statute, because the writing must be signed by the party to be charged; the merchant's confirmation rule applies only to sales of goods under the UCC. The fact that the guaranty would expire 18 months after June 1 is not the reason Decker escapes liability; the suretyship provision alone requires a writing. Baker's demand for payment within one year of the guaranty does not make an oral guaranty enforceable.
questions.explanationJa: 他人の債務を保証する約束（保証契約）は詐欺防止法（statute of frauds）の対象で、保証人が署名した書面がなければ強制できません（保証の主目的が保証人自身の利益である場合を除きます）。Decker はいとこの債務を保証しただけで直接の利益はなく、書面にも署名していないため、責任を負いません。Baker の6月3日の確認書に Decker が異議を述べなかったことは、責任を問われる側の署名がないので要件を満たしません（異議を述べなければ拘束される確認書のルールは、UCC の物品売買で商人間に限られます）。保証が6月1日から18か月で終了する点は、Decker が責任を免れる理由ではありません。保証契約である以上、それだけで書面が必要です。保証から1年以内に支払請求をしたことも、口頭の保証を有効にするものではありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.9

questions.stem: Nolan agreed orally with Train to sell Train a house for $100,000. Train sent Nolan a signed agreement and a down payment of $10,000. Nolan did not sign the agreement, but allowed Train to move into the house. Before closing, Nolan refused to go through with the sale. Train sued Nolan to compel specific performance. Under the provisions of the Statute of Frauds,

choices.label: A
choices.text: Train will win because Train signed the agreement and Nolan did not object.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Train will win because Train made a down payment and took possession.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nolan will win because Nolan did not sign the agreement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nolan will win because the house was worth more than $500.

questions.explanation: A contract for the sale of an interest in land is within the statute of frauds and ordinarily requires a writing signed by the party to be charged. Under the part-performance exception, however, a buyer who has relied on the oral contract, such as by paying part of the price and taking possession with the seller's consent, may obtain specific performance even without the seller's signed writing (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§125, 129). Train paid $10,000 and moved into the house with Nolan's permission, so the oral contract is enforceable against Nolan. Train's signature on the agreement does not help, because the statute requires the signature of the party to be charged, which is Nolan, and Nolan's silence is not a signature. Nolan's failure to sign is overcome by the part-performance exception. The $500 threshold applies to sales of goods under UCC §2-201, not to sales of real estate.
questions.explanationJa: 土地の売買契約は詐欺防止法の対象で、原則として責任を問われる側が署名した書面が必要です。ただし一部履行の例外があり、買主が口頭契約を信頼して代金の一部を支払い、売主の同意のもとで占有を始めた場合には、売主の署名がなくても特定履行を求められます。Train は1万ドルを支払い、Nolan の許可を得て入居しているため、Nolan に対して契約を強制できます。Train が署名していても、必要なのは責任を問われる Nolan の署名であり、Nolan が異議を述べなかったことは署名になりません。Nolan が署名していない点は一部履行の例外で補われます。500ドルの基準は UCC の物品売買に適用されるもので、不動産の売買には関係ありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.10

questions.stem: Kram sent Fargo, a real estate broker, a signed offer to sell a specified parcel of land to Fargo for $250,000. Kram, an engineer, had inherited the land. On the same day that Kram's letter was received, Fargo telephoned Kram and accepted the offer. Which of the following statements is correct under the common law statute of frauds?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No contract could be formed because Fargo's acceptance was oral.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No contract could be formed because Kram's letter was signed only by Kram.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A contract was formed and would be enforceable against both Kram and Fargo.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A contract was formed but would be enforceable only against Kram.

questions.explanation: The statute of frauds does not prevent a contract from being formed; it governs enforceability. A contract for the sale of land is enforceable only against a party who has signed a sufficient writing (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§110, 131, 135). Fargo's oral acceptance of Kram's signed offer formed a contract, and Kram's signed letter, stating the parties, the land, and the price, is a writing signed by Kram, so the contract can be enforced against Kram but not against Fargo, who signed nothing. The claim that no contract could be formed because Fargo's acceptance was oral is wrong because an offer may be accepted orally unless the offer requires otherwise. The claim that no contract could be formed because Kram's letter was signed only by Kram is wrong because a single signature does not prevent formation; it only limits against whom the contract may be enforced. The claim that the contract is enforceable against both Kram and Fargo is wrong because Fargo did not sign any writing.
questions.explanationJa: 詐欺防止法は契約の成立を妨げるものではなく、強制できるかどうかを決めるものです。土地の売買契約は、十分な書面に署名した当事者に対してだけ強制できます。Kram の署名入りの申込みを Fargo が電話で承諾した時点で契約は成立し、当事者・土地・代金を記した Kram の署名入りの手紙があるので、Kram に対しては強制できますが、何にも署名していない Fargo に対しては強制できません。申込みが方法を指定していない限り口頭でも承諾できるため、「承諾が口頭だから契約は成立しない」は誤りです。「Kram しか署名していないから契約は成立しない」も、署名が一方だけでも成立は妨げられず、強制できる相手が限られるだけなので誤りです。Fargo は書面に署名していないため、「両者に強制できる」も誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.11

questions.stem: On May 25, Fresno sold Bronson, a minor, a used computer. On June 1, Bronson reached the age of majority. On June 10, Fresno wanted to rescind the sale. Fresno offered to return Bronson's money and demanded that Bronson return the computer. Bronson refused, claiming that a binding contract existed. Bronson's refusal is

choices.label: A
choices.text: Not justified, because Fresno is not bound by the contract unless Bronson specifically ratifies the contract after reaching the age of majority

choices.label: B
choices.text: Not justified, because Fresno does not have to perform under the contract if Bronson has a right to disaffirm the contract

choices.label: C
choices.text: Justified, because Bronson and Fresno are bound by the contract as of the date Bronson reached the age of majority

choices.label: D
choices.text: Justified, because Fresno must perform under the contract regardless of Bronson's minority

questions.explanation: A contract made by a minor is voidable only at the option of the minor; the adult party is bound and cannot avoid the contract on the ground of the other party's minority (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §14). Fresno, the adult, therefore has no right to rescind the sale, and Bronson may insist on the contract. The statement that Fresno is not bound unless Bronson specifically ratifies after reaching majority is wrong because the adult party is bound from the start; ratification only ends the minor's own power to disaffirm. The statement that Fresno does not have to perform if Bronson has a right to disaffirm is wrong because the power to disaffirm belongs to the minor alone and gives the adult no defense. The statement that both parties became bound as of the date Bronson reached majority is wrong because Fresno was bound from the date of the sale, and Bronson's reaching majority alone, without ratification or a reasonable lapse of time, does not by itself bind Bronson.
questions.explanationJa: 未成年者が結んだ契約は、未成年者の側だけが取り消せる（voidable）契約で、成年の相手方は未成年を理由に契約を免れることはできません。成年者である Fresno には売買を取り消す権利がなく、Bronson は契約の履行を求められます。「Bronson が成年後に追認しない限り Fresno は拘束されない」は、成年の相手方は当初から拘束されている点で誤りです（追認は未成年者自身の取消権を失わせるだけです）。「Bronson に取消権があれば Fresno は履行しなくてよい」も、取消権は未成年者だけのもので、相手方の抗弁にはならないため誤りです。「成年に達した日から両者が拘束される」も、Fresno は売買の時点から拘束されており、Bronson も成年に達しただけで（追認や相当期間の経過なしに）当然に拘束されるわけではないため誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.12

questions.stem: Miller negotiated the sale of Miller's liquor store to Jackson. Jackson asked to see the prior year's financial statements. Using the store's checkbook, Miller prepared a balance sheet and profit and loss statement as well as he could. Miller told Jackson to have an accountant examine Miller's records because Miller was not an accountant. Jackson failed to do so and purchased the store in reliance on Miller's financial statements. Jackson later learned that the financial statements included several errors that resulted in a material overstatement of assets and net income. Miller was not aware that the errors existed. Jackson sued Miller, claiming Miller misrepresented the store's financial condition and that Jackson relied on the financial statements in making the decision to acquire the store. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Jackson will prevail if the errors in the financial statements were material.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Jackson will not prevail because Jackson's reliance on the financial statements was not reasonable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Money damages is the only remedy available to Jackson if, in fact, Miller has committed a misrepresentation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Jackson would be entitled to rescind the purchase even if the errors in the financial statements were not material.

questions.explanation: Miller was unaware of the errors, so any misrepresentation was innocent. To avoid a contract for misrepresentation, the party must show a misstatement of fact that is material (or fraudulent), actual reliance, and reliance that was justified (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§164, 172). Miller warned Jackson that he was not an accountant and told Jackson to have an accountant examine the records; Jackson ignored that warning and relied on statements Miller had prepared from a checkbook, so Jackson's reliance was not justified and Jackson will not prevail. Materiality alone is not enough for Jackson to prevail, because justified reliance is also required. Money damages are not the only remedy for misrepresentation; rescission is the usual remedy for an innocent misrepresentation, and damages are generally reserved for fraud. Rescission is not available for an innocent misrepresentation that was not material.
questions.explanationJa: Miller は誤りに気づいていなかったので、仮に不実表示があっても善意の不実表示（innocent misrepresentation）です。不実表示を理由に契約を取り消すには、重要な（または詐欺的な）事実の誤表示、実際の信頼、そしてその信頼が正当であることが必要です。Miller は自分が会計士ではないと告げ、会計士に記録を確認させるよう勧めていたのに、Jackson はこれを怠り、小切手帳から作った財務諸表を信頼したため、信頼は正当といえず、Jackson は勝訴できません。誤りが重要であるだけでは足りず、正当な信頼も必要なので「重要なら勝訴できる」は誤りです。不実表示の救済は金銭賠償に限られず、善意の不実表示では取消し（rescission）が通常の救済で、損害賠償は主に詐欺の場合に認められます。重要でない善意の誤表示では取消しも認められません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.13

questions.stem: If a person is induced to enter into a contract by another person because of the close relationship between the parties, the contract may be voidable under which of the following defenses?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fraud in the inducement

choices.label: B
choices.text: Unconscionability

choices.label: C
choices.text: Undue influence

choices.label: D
choices.text: Duress

questions.explanation: Undue influence is unfair persuasion of a party who is under the domination of the other party or who, because of their relationship, is justified in assuming that the other will not act against his or her welfare. A contract induced by undue influence is voidable by the victim (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §177). The defense rests on abuse of a close or confidential relationship, which matches the facts described. Fraud in the inducement requires a knowing misrepresentation of a material fact that the other party relies on, not a close relationship. Unconscionability concerns grossly unfair terms or bargaining process and allows a court to refuse enforcement, but it is not based on the relationship between the parties. Duress involves an improper threat that overcomes a party's free will, not persuasion arising from a relationship of trust.
questions.explanationJa: 不当威圧（undue influence）とは、相手方の支配下にある者や、関係性から相手方が自分の利益に反する行動をしないと信じてよい立場にある者に対して、不公正な説得を行うことです。不当威圧によって結ばれた契約は、被害者の側から取り消せます。親密な関係・信頼関係の濫用が要件なので、本問の事実に当てはまります。詐欺（fraud in the inducement）は重要な事実についての故意の虚偽表示とその信頼が要件で、親密な関係を前提にしません。非良心性（unconscionability）は著しく不公正な条件や交渉過程を理由に裁判所が強制を拒むもので、当事者の関係性に基づくものではありません。強迫（duress）は不当な脅しによって自由な意思が奪われる場合で、信頼関係からの説得ではありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.14

questions.stem:
When there has been no performance by either party, which of the following events generally will result in the discharge of a party's obligation to perform as required under the original contract?

Accord and satisfaction | Mutual rescission

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation: Both events discharge the original contract duties. An accord is an agreement to accept a substituted performance in place of the performance originally owed, and satisfaction is the performance of that accord; once the accord is satisfied, the original duty is discharged (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §281). Mutual rescission is an agreement by both parties to cancel the contract; when neither party has performed, each party's promise to give up its rights is consideration for the other's, so the mutual rescission discharges both parties' duties (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §283). Because each event discharges the original obligation, any combination that treats either one as not resulting in a discharge is incorrect.
questions.explanationJa: どちらも元の契約上の義務を消滅させます。代物弁済の合意（accord）は、本来の履行の代わりに別の履行を受け入れる合意で、その合意が履行されると（satisfaction）、元の義務は消滅します。合意解除（mutual rescission）は両当事者が契約の取消しに合意することで、双方とも未履行であれば、互いに権利を放棄する約束がそれぞれの約因となり、両者の義務が消滅します。どちらも元の義務を消滅させるため、いずれか一方でも「消滅しない」とする組み合わせは誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.15

questions.stem: Wren purchased a factory from First Federal Realty. Wren paid 20% at the closing and gave a note for the balance secured by a 20-year mortgage. Five years later, Wren found it increasingly difficult to make payments on the note and defaulted. First Federal threatened to accelerate the loan and foreclose if Wren continued in default. First Federal told Wren to make payment or obtain an acceptable third party to assume the obligation. Wren offered the land to Moss, Inc., for $10,000 less than the equity Wren had in the property. This was acceptable to First Federal and at the closing Moss paid the arrearage, assumed the mortgage and note, and had title transferred to its name. First Federal released Wren. The transaction in question is a(an)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Purchase of land subject to a mortgage

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assignment and delegation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Third party beneficiary contract

choices.label: D
choices.text: Novation

questions.explanation: A novation is a substituted contract in which, with the consent of the obligee, a new party takes the place of an original party and the original obligor is discharged (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §280). First Federal, the creditor, agreed to accept Moss in Wren's place, Moss assumed the mortgage and note, and First Federal released Wren, so the transaction is a novation. A purchase of land subject to a mortgage does not describe this transaction because in that case the buyer does not become personally liable on the note, whereas Moss assumed the note. An assignment and delegation leaves the original obligor (Wren) liable, but First Federal released Wren. A third party beneficiary contract is one made for the benefit of a non-party; it does not describe a creditor agreeing to substitute a new debtor and release the old one.
questions.explanationJa: 更改（novation）とは、債権者の同意のもとで新しい当事者が元の当事者に代わり、元の債務者が免責される新たな契約です。債権者の First Federal が Moss を Wren の代わりとして受け入れ、Moss が抵当権付きの借入と手形を引き受け、First Federal が Wren を免責しているので、この取引は更改です。「抵当権付きのまま土地を購入した（subject to a mortgage）」場合は、買主が手形について個人的な責任を負いませんが、本問の Moss は手形を引き受けています。債権譲渡と債務の委任（assignment and delegation）では元の債務者である Wren の責任が残りますが、本問では Wren は免責されています。第三者のためにする契約は契約外の者に利益を与える契約で、債権者が債務者の交代に同意して旧債務者を免責する本問とは異なります。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.17

questions.stem: Wilcox Co. contracted with Ace Painters Inc. for Ace to paint Wilcox's warehouse. Ace, without advising Wilcox, assigned the contract to Pure Painting Corp. Pure failed to paint Wilcox's warehouse in accordance with the contract specifications. The contract between Ace and Wilcox was silent with regard to a party's right to assign it. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ace remained liable to Wilcox despite the fact that Ace assigned the contract to Pure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ace would not be liable to Wilcox if Ace had notified Wilcox of the assignment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ace's duty to paint Wilcox's warehouse was nondelegable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ace's delegation of the duty to paint Wilcox's warehouse was a breach of the contract.

questions.explanation: A general assignment of 'the contract' is treated as an assignment of rights and a delegation of duties. Delegating a duty does not discharge the delegating party: unless the obligee agrees to a novation, the delegating party remains liable if the delegate fails to perform (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §318(3)). Pure's defective work is therefore Ace's responsibility. Notifying Wilcox of the assignment would not relieve Ace of liability, because only Wilcox's agreement to release Ace (a novation) would do that. Ace's duty to paint the warehouse was delegable because painting a warehouse is not a personal service requiring Ace's special skill and the contract did not prohibit delegation. Because the duty was delegable, Ace's delegation itself was not a breach; the breach was the defective performance.
questions.explanationJa: 「契約」を包括的に譲渡した場合、権利の譲渡と義務の委任（delegation）として扱われます。義務を委任しても委任した者は免責されず、債権者が更改に同意しない限り、受任者が履行しなければ委任者が責任を負います。したがって Pure の不完全な塗装について Ace は Wilcox に責任を負います。Wilcox に譲渡を通知しても、免責には Wilcox の同意（更改）が必要なので Ace は責任を免れません。倉庫の塗装は Ace 固有の技能を要する一身専属的な役務ではなく、契約にも委任の禁止がないため、義務は委任可能です。委任可能な以上、委任自体は契約違反ではなく、違反となるのは不完全な履行です。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.18

questions.stem: Dye sent Hill a written offer to sell a tract of land located in Newtown for $60,000. The parties were engaged in a separate dispute. The offer stated that it would be irrevocable for 60 days if Hill would promise to refrain from suing Dye during this time. Hill promptly delivered a promise not to sue during the term of the offer and to forego suit if Hill accepted the offer. Dye subsequently decided that the possible suit by Hill was groundless and therefore phoned Hill and revoked the offer 15 days after making it. Hill mailed an acceptance on the 20th day. Dye did not reply. Under the circumstances,

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dye's offer was supported by consideration and was not revocable when accepted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dye's written offer would be irrevocable even without consideration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dye's silence was an acceptance of Hill's promise.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dye's revocation, not being in writing, was invalid.

questions.explanation: An offer becomes irrevocable for the stated period (an option contract) when the promise to keep it open is supported by consideration (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §87(1)). Hill's promise to refrain from suing Dye on a claim in a separate dispute is a bargained-for detriment and is consideration; Forbearance from asserting a claim is consideration if the claim is doubtful or is asserted in good faith, so Dye's later view that the suit was groundless does not by itself undo that consideration; nothing in the facts suggests Hill acted in bad faith (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §74). Because the offer was irrevocable for 60 days, Dye's revocation on the 15th day was ineffective, and Hill's acceptance on the 20th day formed a contract. A written offer would not be irrevocable without consideration: the firm-offer rule of UCC §2-205 applies only to merchants' offers to sell goods, and this is a sale of land. Dye's silence was not an acceptance of Hill's promise; Dye's offer itself invited that promise, so no further assent from Dye was needed. The revocation failed because the option was supported by consideration, not because it was oral; a revocation generally need not be in writing.
questions.explanationJa: 申込みを一定期間撤回しないという約束に約因がある場合、その申込みは期間中撤回できないオプション契約になります。別件の紛争で Dye を訴えないという Hill の約束は、取引上の不利益であり約因に当たります。請求を控える約束は、請求に疑義があるか、請求者が善意で権利を主張している限り約因になるため、後になって Dye が訴訟は根拠がないと考えただけでは約因は失われません（問題文に Hill の悪意を示す事実はありません）。申込みは60日間撤回できなかったため、15日目の撤回は無効で、20日目の Hill の承諾で契約が成立します。約因がなくても書面の申込みなら撤回できないというルール（firm offer）は、UCC 上の商人による物品売買の申込みに限られ、土地の売買には適用されません。Dye の沈黙が Hill の約束を承諾したわけでもなく、Dye の申込み自体がその約束を求めていたので、追加の同意は不要です。撤回が無効なのは約因があるからで、口頭だからではありません（撤回は通常、書面でなくてもかまいません）。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.19

questions.stem: Carson agreed orally to repair Ives' rare book for $450. Before the work was started, Ives asked Carson to perform additional repairs to the book and agreed to increase the contract price to $650. After Carson completed the work, Ives refused to pay and Carson sued. Ives' defense was based on the Statute of Frauds. What total amount will Carson recover?
questions.explanation: The contract is for services (repairing a book), not for the sale of goods, so UCC §2-201's $500 writing requirement does not apply, and the repairs could be performed within one year, so the contract is not within the common-law statute of frauds either (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §110). The oral agreement and its oral modification are therefore enforceable. The modification raising the price to $650 is supported by consideration because Carson agreed to perform additional repairs he was not previously obligated to do (Restatement (Second) of Contracts §73). Carson recovers the full $650. Recovering $0 would require the statute of frauds to bar the contract, which it does not. Recovering $200 or $450 would ignore that the modified agreement, supported by new consideration, replaced the original $450 price.
questions.explanationJa: 本の修理は役務の契約で物品売買ではないため、UCC の500ドル以上の書面要件は適用されず、修理は1年以内に履行できるので、コモンロー上の詐欺防止法の対象にもなりません。したがって口頭の契約もその口頭の変更も有効です。代金を650ドルに上げる変更には、Carson が本来義務のない追加修理を引き受けたという約因があります。Carson は650ドル全額を回収できます。0ドルとなるのは詐欺防止法で契約が強制できない場合ですが、本問は該当しません。200ドルや450ドルとするのは、新たな約因に支えられた変更後の合意が当初の450ドルの代金に置き換わったことを無視しています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Contracts Q.20
